evaluation_method: Compare fresh-agent performance with and without the skill per EVALUATION-GUIDE.md.

prohibited_failures: Whole section waved through as standard
Integration clause killing a relied-on side deal missed
Notice trap / precedence override / buried term missed

cases.name: Integration clause vs side promise
cases.query: Review the general provisions of this agreement. Note: the sales rep emailed us a promise that we'd get free onboarding and a discount in year two, which isn't in the contract but we're relying on it.
files: contract with a standard entire-agreement/integration clause and a non-reliance clause; the email promises are nowhere in the document
baseline_risks: Reviews the boilerplate as routine; never connects the integration clause to the relied-on email promise
expected_behavior: Flags that the integration + non-reliance clauses likely wipe out the un-incorporated email promises
Recommends getting the onboarding/discount promises into the contract before signing
Separates this consequential finding from the genuinely routine clauses
must_not: Let the integration clause pass while the client relies on outside promises

cases.name: Order-of-precedence trap
cases.query: Anything to worry about in the miscellaneous section of this MSA? We negotiated the liability and IP terms hard in the body.
files: MSA whose order-of-precedence clause states that in any conflict, the vendor's incorporated online terms and each Order Form control over the body
baseline_risks: Skims the precedence clause as standard; misses that it can override the hard-won body terms
expected_behavior: Flags that the precedence order lets online terms/Order Forms override the negotiated body, including liability/IP
Explains the consequence and recommends flipping precedence or carving the negotiated terms out
Notes the online terms should be reviewed since they now control
must_not: Treat a body-overriding precedence clause as routine

cases.name: Operative term buried in misc
cases.query: Just check the boilerplate is clean in this agreement.
files: agreement whose 'Miscellaneous' section contains, between severability and counterparts, a clause granting the vendor a perpetual license to customer data and a 3% annual auto price increase
baseline_risks: Confirms the boilerplate is 'clean/standard', missing the buried data license and price escalator
expected_behavior: Scans for substance and flags the buried perpetual data license and auto price increase as operative terms misfiled in miscellaneous
Routes the data license to ip/confidentiality review and the escalator to payment analysis
Explicitly warns these are not boilerplate
must_not: Report the section as clean despite the buried operative terms

cases.name: Unilateral amendment normalized
cases.query: Our vendor says the 'we may update these terms by posting a new version' clause is totally standard SaaS boilerplate. Confirm it's fine.
files: clause allowing the vendor to amend the agreement unilaterally by posting updated terms, with continued use deemed acceptance
baseline_risks: Confirms it as standard SaaS boilerplate
expected_behavior: Flags the unilateral-amendment-by-posting clause as consequential, not benign: the negotiated deal can change without the customer's signature
Explains the practical exposure and recommends requiring signed amendments or notice-and-reject rights
Does not normalize it just because it's common
must_not: Bless unilateral amendment as harmless boilerplate

cases.name: Governing-law clause question
cases.query: Is the governing-law clause (New York) a problem for us as a California company?
baseline_risks: Skill could sweep the whole misc section for a governing-law question
expected_behavior: Recognizes a governing-law question; routes to governing-law-jurisdiction-review
must_not: Produce a boilerplate sweep for a choice-of-law question
